title: Establishing model credibility for a dental implant under osseointegration loading: Two implicit FEA models across two mechanisms using a numeric evidence scale
runhead: Credibility of implant FEA for early loading
device: Endosseous dental implant with internal connection and healing abutment

models.name: Micro-Region Interface Model (MRIM)
models.what_it_computes: Implicit finite element simulation of a local peri-implant bone region with explicit thread geometry and a bonded interface surrogate to compute interfacial micromotion, peri-implant strain energy density, and cortical crest principal strains.

models.name: Segmental Jaw Continuum Model (SJCM)
models.what_it_computes: Implicit finite element simulation of a mandibular segment with heterogeneous cortical–trabecular bone to compute global implant–bone construct stiffness, abutment displacement, and cortical load transfer under functional loading.

mechanisms.name: Axial centric loading during early healing
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Vertical occlusal force on a recently placed implant can drive interfacial motion and bulk bone strains that affect primary stability and early tissue remodeling.

mechanisms.name: Oblique lateral excursion during early healing
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Off-axis shear and bending during parafunctional or lateral movements can localize stress at the crestal cortical margin and challenge the developing bone–implant interface.

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored per model–mechanism pair on a 0–4 evidence scale (0=insufficient, 1=limited, 2=adequate, 3=strong, 4=extensive).
